proposed_from.topic: Semiparametric efficiency and cross-fitted one-step inference for the smooth quadratic conditional-optimal-transport lower bound on mean squared individual treatment effects in observational studies: extend Lin-Gao-Blanchet-Glynn (arXiv:2602.20681, Proposition 3.3 and Theorem 3.2) from randomized marginal-sample asymptotic normality to i.i.d. observational data under ignorability and overlap by deriving the observed-data canonical gradient, efficiency bound, propensity-corrected wavelet-Brenier one-step estimator, uniform studentized normality and Wald coverage, with Ji-Lei-Spector's 401(k) SIPP analysis as the applied consumer
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest published result is Lin et al. (2026), whose Theorem 3.2 is a pointwise randomized marginal-sample limit and whose conclusion leaves covariate-dependent propensity scores open. Ji et al. (2024) are the closest observational result, but their AIPW correction is for fitted dual bounds and its robust validity can be conservative. The proposed theorem-level gap is therefore neither a relabeling of Lin's limit nor an AIPW restatement: it is the observed-data canonical gradient, semiparametric efficiency bound, and uniform studentized one-step law for the sharp smooth primal COT lower endpoint.

seed_details.seed: Observed-data canonical gradient for the sharp smooth quadratic COT endpoint
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from randomized-arm linearization because inverse-propensity weighting is routine.
seed_details.rebuttal: The COT value depends jointly on conditional outcome laws and the covariate law, so the observed-data tangent projection and the cancellation-safe one-step value are not supplied by either paper.

seed_details.seed: Uniform studentized Wald inference for the sharp observational COT endpoint
seed_details.anchor: lin2026statistical, Theorem 3.2 and Remark 3.3; ji2024modelagnostic, Theorem 3.6
seed_details.red_team: A uniform CLT follows automatically from a pointwise DML expansion.
seed_details.rebuttal: Uniformity must control Brenier stability, nuisance products, and a variance lower bound simultaneously; Ji--Lei--Spector obtain conservative lower-confidence validity rather than this exact studentized claim.

seed_details.seed: Adaptive inference at the vanishing-variance conditional-transport frontier
seed_details.red_team: This is just the ordinary second-order delta method for Wasserstein distance.
seed_details.rebuttal: The conditional Brenier derivative, ignorability score, and learned propensity interact along local equality sequences; no located result treats all three.

seed_details.seed: Overlap-boundary weighted remainder theory for observational COT
seed_details.red_team: Fixed overlap already removes the boundary, so the seed changes the problem.
seed_details.rebuttal: It is a distinct weakening of the present fixed-overlap regime and requires a new weighted differentiability argument.

seed_details.red_team: A bias--variance choice for regularization is routine.
seed_details.rebuttal: A derived observational frontier would require a nontrivial joint regularization-bias and propensity-score expansion, but no supplied anchor establishes the necessary regularized COT derivative.

seed_details.seed: Efficiency comparison between primal COT and observational dual bounds
seed_details.red_team: Primal and dual values agree by Kantorovich duality.
seed_details.rebuttal: Population value equality does not imply equality of fitted estimators or influence functions, but a derived divergence frontier was not credible from the available dual regularity theory.

seed_details.red_team: The endpoint is a distributional heterogeneity bound, not a policy-value functional.
seed_details.rebuttal: No supplied anchor yields a policy class and welfare target whose regret is governed by this endpoint without adding a separate decision problem.

seed_details.seed: Permutation inversion for observational COT bounds
seed_details.red_team: Observational treatment assignment supplies no exchangeability orbit.
seed_details.rebuttal: Ignorability alone is insufficient for a finite-sample permutation group, and no covariate-conditional exact symmetry is available in the anchor.

proposed_from.literature_map: Lin--Gao--Blanchet--Glynn establish smooth-density wavelet COT estimation, quadratic stability, and a pointwise randomized-sample central limit theorem; their conclusion explicitly names covariate-dependent propensities and observational ignorability as future work. Ji--Lei--Spector give cross-fitted observational augmentation for dual COT bounds and use the 401(k) SIPP application, but their valid confidence bound may retain dual slack. Manole--Balakrishnan--Niles-Weed--Wasserman provide the smooth strongly convex Brenier stability ancestor for linearizing a squared transport value. Chernozhukov et al. and Newey--Robins provide the orthogonal-score and cross-fitting remainder templates. The closest unresolved intersection is an observed-data canonical gradient and uniform studentization for the sharp smooth primal endpoint.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Conjecture 2 regular regime
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Efficient inference is conditional on fixed overlap, compact smooth bounded arm densities, conditional strong-Brenier regularity, positive efficiency variance, and the separately attained clipped-propensity rate.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Uniform efficient studentized normality and Wald coverage only for the stated regular observed-law and learner-rate regime; equality and vanishing-variance sequences are excluded.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Open-ended Question 1
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The first-order Wald result deliberately does not cover the equality/vanishing-efficiency-boundary regime.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Inference along sequences with sigma_n tending to zero is reserved for the explicit second-order conditional-transport question.

banked_reason: Independent referee re-grade: subfield, not field. The headline efficiency/DML theorem is the propensity-corrected version of Lin-Gao-Blanchet-Glynn arXiv:2602.20681 (Prop 3.3 + Thm 3.2: same conditional estimand, same centered-Kantorovich-potential influence function, same s > D/2 condition; cited by the note) composed with Manole et al. AoS 2024 Lemma 21/Thm 22, i.e. exactly the one-step correction the cited literature names as its own future work; the single open question (degeneracy-adaptive inference) is unresolved.
